text:
marco: hey — running into a weird hang when cancelling retrofit calls in our kotlin sampleapp on Pixel 8 (Android 14). coroutine cancels but the okhttp call seems to keep a connection and next request blocks. anyone seen this? :thinking_face:
sofia: ugh, that sounds nasty. does it repro on emulator or only device?
marco: only on device so far, but i can repro on a physical Pixel 8 + company VPN. emulator seems fine.
james: can you paste the coroutine + retrofit call pattern? are you using call.enqueue or suspend fun with await?
marco: using a suspend extension that does: withContext(io) { service.doThing() } where doThing is a Retrofit suspend function. when i cancel the parent job we do job.cancelAndJoin() and then start another request immediately, which then stalls for ~20s.
sofia: hmm can you share the okhttp config? keepalive? connection pool settings?
marco: default client from our SDK. we set connectTimeout(10, TimeUnit.SECONDS) and readTimeout(0, TimeUnit.SECONDS) (streaming), no explicit callTimeout.
marco: here's a small repro snippet:
```kotlin
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder().build()
val retrofit = Retrofit.Builder().client(client).build()
// suspend fun service.doThing(): Response
val job = launch(Dispatchers.IO) { service.doThing() }
job.cancel()
// immediately start another request
service.doThing()
```
sofia: looks similar to a connection-pool/idle-connection eviction race i've seen. cancel doesn't always close the socket if it's in IO, so next connect might reuse a half-closed connection.
dev-bot: Incident bot: linked issue created: #5143 "OkHttp reuse on cancel causes next request stall on Pixel"
james: one quick try — set callTimeout(30, TimeUnit.SECONDS) and also client.connectionPool().evictAll() after cancel as a hack to see if reuse is the cause.
marco: tried evictAll() after cancel — it improves but not fully. also adding call.cancel() inside cancel handler seems to avoid the stall.
liya: could also be TLS session reuse + vpn MTU causing a stuck FIN. have you tried toggling keepAlive(false) or set pingInterval for HTTP/2?
marco: toggling keepAlive off made it much better. that seems to confirm connection reuse is culprit. but we can't leave keepalive off for perf.
sofia: ok, if keepalive triggers it might be platform-specific. can you capture tcpdump or okhttp event listener logs?
marco: attaching logs in thread — shows socket in CLOSE_WAIT for long time.
james: probable mitigation for SDK: expose a configurable callTimeout and expose a small helper to cancel underlying call when coroutine cancelled. sample patch idea: add a suspend wrapper that registers coroutine.invokeOnCancellation { call.cancel() } before await.
liya: agreed — also add a note in onboarding docs about Pixel vpn weirdness and default keepalive caveat.
marco: i'll draft a tiny PR with wrapper and a unit test repro (instrumented device test). opening draft now. thx y'all :raised_hands:
sofia: nice, please link PR in the issue. marking as triage-needed. :thumbsup:
marco: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/1307 (draft) — includes helper and docs note.
dev-bot: CI queue: presubmit checks started for pr/1307
james: great, once CI green let's ship as opt-in in the next patch and consider making it default after more infra tests.
marco: sounds good, will add an integration test matrix for Pixel 7/8 + vpn combos.
sofia: awesome. saved a screenshot for the docs.
liya: leaving a reaction :lock: on the docs note for security/privileged network mention.
marco: thanks folks. will update issue when draft ready for review.
